title: Universal grace is an external benefit; particular grace works within
source_text: XXXIII. Ex dictis vero satis patet, Theologos istos nomine gratiae universalis non intelligere gratiam aliquam in hominibus inhaerentem, sed tantum externum quoddam Dei beneficium, quo filium morti tradidit, ut divinae justitiae pro peccatis omnium hominum satisfieret, & quo justitia ejus ita pacata, homines extrinsecus vocat ad communionem salutis, quam Christus illis morte sua peperit. Et contra per gratiam particularem illos praecipue designare dona & auxilia Dei, quibus intus in hominibus agens in illis conversionem & fidem operatur, illosque tandem reipsa salutis aeternae participes efficit.
pass_a_gloss: XXXIII. But from what has been said it is plain enough, that those Theologians by the name of universal grace do not understand some grace inhering in men, but only a certain external benefit of God, by which he delivered his son to death, that satisfaction might be made to divine justice for the sins of all men, and by which his justice being thus appeased, he calls men externally to the communion of salvation, which Christ obtained for them by his death. And on the contrary by particular grace they chiefly designate the gifts and helps of God, by which acting inwardly in men he works conversion and faith in them, and at last makes them in fact partakers of eternal salvation.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXXIII. From what has been said it is clear enough that these theologians do not mean by universal grace any grace inhering in people. They mean only an external benefit of God: he handed his Son over to death so that divine justice might be satisfied for the sins of all, and, his justice being thus appeased, he calls people from outside to share in the salvation that Christ won for them by his death.

By particular grace, on the other hand, they chiefly mean the gifts and helps of God by which he acts within people, works conversion and faith in them, and in the end makes them actually share in eternal salvation.
